obfaryn-api/com.peco2282.obfaryn.api.ann.source: Public reader for Obfaryn policy annotations, usable by host-loaded extension passes without depending on the core engine.

Annotations are interpreted directly from ASM nodes by descriptor, so neither the annotation classes nor this helper's host need be on the runtime classpath. Both runtime-visible and runtime-invisible annotations are recognized. Queries only inspect their supplied nodes; ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ must be called separately to reject conflicts.

obfaryn-api/com.peco2282.obfaryn.api.con.source: Represents a resource entry consisting of a name and associated binary data.
The ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ class is used to store and manage entries of resources, where each resource is uniquely identified by its name and holds an array of binary data.

Equality between two instances of ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ is determined by comparing both their ZXQOBFARYN1QXZ values and the contents of the ZXQOBFARYN2QXZ arrays. The custom implementation of ZXQOBFARYN3QXZ ensures that two resource entries are considered equal only if their names and binary data are identical. Similarly, the ZXQOBFARYN4QXZ function is overridden to generate hash codes based on both properties.
This class is typically utilized in contexts where resources are identified by a string key and need to be stored, retrieved, or modified in bulk.

ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ is retained and exposed without copying. Mutating it changes content-based equality and the hash code, so do not modify the array while this entry is a hash-based collection key. The generated ZXQOBFARYN1QXZ also shares the array unless a replacement is supplied; use ZXQOBFARYN2QXZ for an independent byte array.
Raw resource bytes shared with the caller, without encoding assumptions.
Archive-relative resource path, such as ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ; no validation is performed here.

ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ is a full-match regex over the ORIGINAL ZXQOBFARYN1QXZ identity (never the renamed/obfuscated one). When several rules match the same method, later rules in the configured list override earlier ones on a per-property basis: a later rule that leaves ZXQOBFARYN2QXZ at ZXQOBFARYN3QXZ does not clear an earlier rule's explicit choice.

Put broad defaults first and narrow exceptions last, since the later rule wins where they overlap. For example, dispatch-obfuscate control flow across a package, but spare one hot method and give it a latency budget:

Both rules match ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ; because the specific rule is later it wins per property, so ZXQOBFARYN1QXZ ends up with numbers off and control flow NONE while every other ZXQOBFARYN2QXZ method keeps DISPATCH. A rule only overrides the properties it sets — the broad rule's DISPATCH stands wherever the specific rule leaves ZXQOBFARYN3QXZ at ZXQOBFARYN4QXZ.

The single reader/writer for the textual mapping format, so no caller re-implements the syntax.

Lines: a class is ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ at the left margin; a method is an indented ZXQOBFARYN1QXZ; a field is an indented ZXQOBFARYN2QXZ; a relocated package is ZXQOBFARYN3QXZ at the left margin. Configuration interface for specifying obfuscation exclusion (keep) rules.

ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ provides a fluent API for platforms and plugins to define which classes, members (methods and fields), packages, and resources should be preserved from obfuscation. Class and owner names may use dotted or JVM internal form; method descriptors must use JVM descriptor syntax. Keep rules describe preservation requirements, not byte-for-byte output guarantees: references may still need updating when other declarations are renamed. In the core implementation, keep rules preserve names but do not disable method-body passes or virtualization. Keeping fields also prevents their constant values from being moved into class initialization. Use ZXQOBFARYN1QXZ for virtualization-specific exclusions.
Preserves the name of a specific method, identified by owner, name, and descriptor. This does not automatically preserve the owner class name or suppress body transformations.
Preserves class and member names within the specified package. The core implementation includes subpackages as well as the named package itself.

This rule does not create the resource, rewrite references in its contents, or preserve classes named inside it; add the corresponding class or member rules separately.

obfaryn-standard/com.peco2282.obfaryn.st.source: One artifact of a cross-artifact assembly: its paths, its stable id, and its own body-pass ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ (platform selection, string/number/control-flow choices, flags, body seed).

The config's renaming switches are not used here — renaming is decided once for the whole program by ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ, not per artifact. Per-artifact ZXQOBFARYN1QXZ/ZXQOBFARYN2QXZ are rejected, because those passes must run after renaming and renaming is global (see §8.3).

Body-pass package selection is per artifact, mirroring single-artifact ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ: ZXQOBFARYN1QXZ starts this artifact from an empty pipeline instead of the standard recipe, and ZXQOBFARYN2QXZ names additional provider-supplied packages (resolved on the host/extension classloader). The global rename runs regardless; any renamer a selected package registers is dropped, as for the standard one.

Names are global and owned by the session: one keep set, one hierarchy, one rename, one mapping. Bodies, resources and I/O are local to each artifact. The run has three phases over a shared ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ:
Phase A (per artifact): read the JAR, run platform detection/configuration against the whole-program view, collect manifest/service/platform keep rules, and run every body pass except renaming.
Phase B (once): union every artifact's classes into one ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ and run a single ZXQOBFARYN1QXZ over it, producing the global mapping.
Phase C (per artifact): split the renamed union back out by origin, remap each artifact's ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ, and write its JAR.

Writing the JARs is not atomic: a mid-run failure can leave only some of them written. This is not the distribution model where an obfuscated API is shipped and rebuilt later; it requires every artifact to be present at assembly time.

platforms/mc-mod/com.peco2282.obfaryn.pl.source: Shared behavior for the Minecraft mod-loader platforms (Fabric, Forge, NeoForge).

Detection and entrypoint discovery work from the compiled classes and the loader's own metadata resource (ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ, ZXQOBFARYN1QXZ, ZXQOBFARYN2QXZ) without the loader jars on the classpath. Each loader resolves its mod/entrypoint classes by the names written in those resources, so ZXQOBFARYN3QXZ keeps the resources verbatim and keeps the entrypoint class names. A loader whose hot callbacks are annotation-driven (Forge/NeoForge's ZXQOBFARYN4QXZ) declares that annotation in ZXQOBFARYN5QXZ; those handlers and the methods they call are kept as plain bytecode. Nothing here infers a hot path from a method name such as ZXQOBFARYN6QXZ.

Fabric mods ship a root ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ and implement one of Fabric's initializer interfaces (ZXQOBFARYN1QXZ, ZXQOBFARYN2QXZ, ZXQOBFARYN3QXZ), named in that file. Fabric event callbacks are registered as lambdas rather than annotated, so no method is excluded from virtualization by this platform.

Forge mods declare a ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ-annotated class (ZXQOBFARYN1QXZ) and a ZXQOBFARYN2QXZ descriptor. ZXQOBFARYN3QXZ handlers are kept as plain bytecode. Detection from ZXQOBFARYN4QXZ alone is reported only when the NeoForge descriptor is absent, so a NeoForge archive is not misread as Forge.

NeoForge mods declare a ZXQOBFARYN0QXZ-annotated class (ZXQOBFARYN1QXZ) and a ZXQOBFARYN2QXZ descriptor. ZXQOBFARYN3QXZ handlers (NeoForge's own event bus) are kept as plain bytecode. The NeoForge-specific annotation and descriptor keep this distinct from ZXQOBFARYN4QXZ.
